app.name: Company Brain
app.tagline: Build a searchable brain from your own documents.

home.title: Home
home.intro: What this installation holds, and what it has done recently. These figures cover the whole project, not one library.
home.offline: The services are not running, so there is nothing to count yet. Start them and this screen fills in.
home.emptyProject: No libraries yet. Import a document and it appears here.
home.graphUnavailable: The graph could not be reached, so the figures derived from it are shown as unavailable rather than as zero. They are two different facts.
home.pagesHelp: Nothing records a page count yet: a version is registered before the document has been extracted, so the number is not knowable at that point.
home.activityUnavailable: The catalog could not be read, so recent activity is unknown.

stack.title: Backing services
stack.intro: Company Brain runs its vector database, workflow engine and catalog locally in Docker. Nothing is indexed until you start these and approve a run.
stack.devMode: Dev mode — the worker image is built from the local source tree.
stack.stopNotice: Stopping removes the containers but keeps every volume, so your vectors and catalog survive.

styles.title: Answer wording
styles.intro: How developed an answer should be at each effort level. The rules that keep every answer grounded in your documents are not editable here and always win.
styles.unavailable: The answer wording could not be read.

docker.missingBody: Company Brain runs its services in Docker. Install Docker Desktop (Windows and macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux), start it, and try again.

health.title: Service health
health.unavailable: The control API has not answered yet. Start the stack first.

ping.title: End-to-end check
ping.intro: Runs a workflow through Temporal onto the worker, which probes Qdrant and Postgres. This proves the whole path, not just that the containers exist.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.workspaceNotNative: Choose a workspace inside your Linux home directory. Windows drive mounts under /mnt lose file permissions and run far slower, which Postgres and Qdrant report as corruption.
error.composeFailed: Docker Compose refused the command. The service logs below usually say why.
error.controlUnreachable: The control API did not answer. It may still be starting — wait a moment and refresh.
error.unsupportedFormat: This format is not supported yet. V1 reads PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, TXT and Markdown.
error.providerUnconfigured: No Gemini project is configured. Set BRAIN_GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and make sure Application Default Credentials are available.
error.runNotFound: That run no longer exists. Temporal keeps history for a limited period; start the import again.
error.graphUnreachable: The graph is not answering. Start the stack from the Services tab and try again.
error.badIdentifier: That identifier does not name anything in the graph. It may be from a document that was re-indexed.
error.sourcePathUnknown: That document was imported before the catalog stored its file path, so it cannot reindex itself. Import it again from the original file.
error.rebuildUnavailable: No run still holds this document's artifacts, so there is nothing to replay without paying again.
error.documentNotFound: That document is no longer in this library. Another window may have removed it — refresh the list.
error.questionNotFound: That question is no longer in flight. Questions live in the control API's memory and are lost if it restarts — ask it again.
error.controlTimeout: The control API is running but did not finish in time. That is not a stack still coming up — check the API's logs, and if you have just rebuilt one half of the app, rebuild the other.
error.controlStreamStalled: The turn behind it keeps going and lands in the conversation either way, so nothing was lost and nothing needs asking twice. Open the conversation again to see how it ended.
error.notSignedIn: Sign in to the paid service before using it, or switch back to the local backend.
error.unauthenticated: The session is no longer valid. Sign in again.
error.unknownUser: That identity is genuine but has no account here yet. An operator has to add it.
error.noMembership: This account does not belong to that organisation.
error.tenantRequired: This account belongs to more than one organisation, and this release works with one. An operator has to leave a single active membership in place.
error.tenantScopePending: This organisation's corpus is managed by the local backend, which writes to the volume directly, so the paid service has no inbox to put a file in. Switch to the local backend to import into it, or sign in to an organisation of your own.
error.notAVideoUrl: That link is not a single YouTube video. Playlists and channels are not expanded — paste each video's own link.
error.ytdlpMissing: This installation cannot download from YouTube itself. Reinstall the app, or set BRAIN_YTDLP to a yt-dlp binary.
error.youtubeRefusedThisMachine: YouTube refused this computer, not the video. It asked to sign in — usually a sign of too many requests in a short time. Wait a few minutes and try again.
error.youtubeTimedOut: YouTube did not answer this computer in time. Check the connection and try again.
error.videoUnavailable: YouTube will not serve this video: it may be private, deleted, age-restricted or blocked in this country.
error.videoIsLive: A live stream has no duration and no end, so there is nothing to index yet. Try again once the recording is published.
error.audioUnavailable: This video has no captions, so its audio has to be downloaded, and YouTube would not serve it to this computer.
error.resolutionNotTrusted: The video details did not match the link. Try pasting the link again.
error.audioFormatUnsupported: The audio came back in a container Amazon Transcribe cannot read, and this product does not re-encode it.
error.artifactNotFound: That file is not there to download. Only a book can be fetched this way, and only from a run that produced one.
error.artifactChanged: The file on disk no longer matches what the catalog recorded for it, so it is not the book this run produced. Build it again.
error.epubSourceMissing: No run still holds this version's chunks, so there is nothing to compose a book from. Reindexing restores them, but pays for correction again.
error.notAChannelUrl: That link is not a YouTube channel. A link to a video is imported from the Import screen.
error.youtubeKeyMissing: No YouTube Data API key. Set one on the Services screen; it is kept in the OS keychain.
error.youtubeQuotaExceeded: The day's YouTube API quota is gone. It resets at midnight Pacific; the key is fine.
error.youtubeRefused: The YouTube API refused the key or the request. Check the key exists and that YouTube Data API v3 is enabled on that project.
error.youtubeUnreachable: Could not reach the YouTube API. Check the connection.
error.channelNotSynced: That channel has not been synced yet. Paste its link and press Sync.
error.libraryOwnedByAnother: That library belongs to another organisation.

library.title: Library
library.intro: Documents indexed in this library. A version becomes answerable only once every projection has completed.
library.includeAbsent: Show documents whose file is missing
library.empty: Nothing indexed yet. Import a document to begin.

confirm.title: Permanently remove “{{title}}”
confirm.body: This deletes its Qdrant vectors, its graph nodes and {{versions}} version(s) from the catalog. There is no undo.
confirm.kept: Kept: the run history, what it cost, and the original file on disk.

library.cannotReindex: This document was imported before the catalog recorded a source path, so it cannot be reindexed. Import it again from the file.
library.cannotRebuild: No run still holds this document's chunks, so there is nothing to replay. Reindexing works, but pays for correction again.
library.startedReindex: Reindex started ({{id}}). It stops at the approval gate before spending.
library.startedRebuild: Rebuild started ({{id}}). Only embedding can spend, and it asks first.
library.removed: Removed: {{points}} Qdrant points, {{chunks}} graph chunks, {{versions}} version(s).
library.removedKeptVersions: {{count}} version(s) still exist because another document shares them.
library.removedKept: The run history, the costs and the file on disk are kept.

scores.basis: {{questions}} generated questions over {{chunks}} chunks · {{misses}} did not find their own chunk. The questions are written from the passages they must find, so the dense-only figure is what the lexical leg is worth without that leakage; the noise floor is what an off-topic query scores.

stats.agree: The catalog, the graph and the vector index agree on the chunk count.
stats.disagree: The three stores disagree about how many chunks this version has. A re-index that produced fewer chunks can leave the previous tail behind.
stats.spans: {{verified}} of {{chunks}} spans still hold their own text in {{stream}}.
stats.coverage: {{percent}}% of the stream is covered by a chunk.
stats.status: What the document does with them:
stats.diverged: does not match what the run produced
stats.namesFolded: {{names}} names were extracted and fold to {{concepts}} concepts: accents and punctuation are stripped for matching, so two spellings are one node.
stats.staleQuotes: {{count}} claim(s) left by an earlier run carry a quote their chunk no longer contains. They read exactly like good ones.
stats.floorHonest: The similarity floor is {{min}} and a wrong chunk scores {{noise}}, so the floor discriminates.
stats.floorBelowNoise: The similarity floor is {{min}} but a wrong chunk scores {{noise}} — the floor admits what it was measured to exclude.
stats.chargedTwice: Charged in more than one run: {{stages}}. A stage billed twice was paid for doing something over.
stats.priceCaveat: Prices are third-party multipliers over measured token counts, not an invoice.
stats.profileCollision: The heading rules were inherited from “{{profile}}”.
stats.overlapUnknown: There is no evidence to judge the overlap from, which is not the same as no overlap.

library.cannotBuildEpub: No run still holds this version's chunks, so there is nothing to compose a book from.
library.metadataAuthorHint: Leave empty if the document has none.
library.metadataWhy: The title starts as the file's own name and the author starts empty. Whatever you type here stands: nothing overwrites it afterwards.

import.title: Import a document
import.intro: Everything up to the approval gate is free: the document is extracted and chunked so you can see what would be indexed before anything is paid for.
import.stageCorrect: Correct the text (the most expensive stage)
import.stageReview: Review the correction before the rest of the spend
import.dropHint: Drag a document here, or choose one with the button.
import.videoHint: Paste YouTube links, one per line. Each one becomes its own import, with its own gate.

fetch.resolving: Asking YouTube about this video, from this computer…
fetch.downloading: Downloading the audio, because this video has no captions…
fetch.uploading: Sending the audio to the service…

import.stageBuildEpub: Build an EPUB to download (nearly free)

queue.title: Imports
queue.empty: Nothing has been imported into this library yet.
queue.gateComing: Reading the document — the estimate appears here when it is ready.

errorKind.audio_unavailable: The audio could not be downloaded, so there is nothing to transcribe.
errorKind.fetch_worker_unavailable: Nobody picked the download task up. The worker that talks to YouTube is not running.
errorKind.video_has_no_duration: The video does not declare a duration, so nothing can be estimated from it.
errorKind.video_is_live: A live stream has no duration and no end, so there is nothing to index yet.
errorKind.video_unavailable: YouTube will not serve this video: it may be private, deleted, or unavailable in this country.
errorKind.youtube_refused_this_host: YouTube refused this server, not the video. It is asking the machine that downloads to sign in — usually because that address is a datacentre. The video itself is fine.

queue.activateDone: Published. {{count}} document(s) now answer from this version.
queue.activateWhy: Everything was indexed and paid for; only the promotion was withheld, because the inherited heading rules and the built-in ones disagreed about this document's structure. Publishing it costs nothing and can be undone by promoting another version.

gate.title: Approve before spending
gate.intro: Nothing has been paid for yet. These figures are projected from measured token counts.
gate.notFinal: Correction changes the text's length, so these are not the chunks that will be indexed.
gate.profileCollision: This document shares a structural fingerprint with another family
gate.profileDefault: No profile exists for this family of documents yet.
gate.profileWillLearn: One will be learned after approval, and every later document of this family inherits it for free.
gate.profileNoLearn: The engine's built-in rules will be used. They were measured on a real book, so this is a known-good setting rather than a gap.
gate.profileChoice: What should this document be chunked with?
gate.profileCollisionHelp: The fingerprint is structural, not topical, so two unrelated families with the same layout match exactly. A low overlap is the case to look at.

video.title: Approve this video
video.intro: Nothing has been paid for yet. Transcription and correction start only when you approve.

captions.manual: the video's own captions ({{language}}), written by a person — free
captions.auto: YouTube's automatic captions ({{language}}) — free, and unpunctuated

video.transcribe: none published, so Amazon Transcribe will read the audio — this is what costs
video.noPreview: There are no captions to read, so there is no text to preview until the transcription is paid for. The figures below are projected from the video's length through a speech rate that has not been measured yet, and the range is wide for that reason.
video.correctAuto: Automatic captions arrive with no punctuation, which is what correction is good at repairing — so it starts on. It is also the stage that dominates the bill, and its value on a transcript has not been measured.
video.correctManual: A person already wrote and punctuated these captions, so correction starts off: its value on a transcript has not been measured and it is the stage that dominates the bill.
video.correctTranscribe: Amazon punctuates its own output, so correction starts off: its value on a transcript has not been measured and it is the stage that dominates the bill.

ask.title: Ask the library
ask.intro: Answers come only from indexed documents, and every assertion carries a citation you can check.
ask.question: Question
ask.placeholder: What do these documents say about…?
ask.offCorpus: This question is not about this library
ask.spentUnpriced: Token counts were recorded; some models have no listed price.
ask.historyEmpty: Nothing asked yet. This history lives in the window and goes when it reloads.
ask.nothingSelected: Ask something, or pick an earlier question.
ask.noAnswerYet: Citations appear here once a question has been answered.
ask.noEvidence: This citation names a fragment that is not among the retrieved passages, so there is nothing to show beside it.
ask.notCitedInsufficient: These passages were retrieved and did not support an answer. They are what this library does have on the question.
ask.notCitedOffCorpus: These came nearest without clearing the similarity floor. If they look unrelated, the question belongs to another library; if they look right, the floor is too high.
ask.keepsRunning: it keeps running if you leave this tab or close the window

chat.title: Conversation
chat.intro: Ask a follow-up and it is understood in context: the question is rewritten to stand on its own before the library is searched, and every answer still carries citations you can check.
chat.listEmpty: No conversations on this shelf yet.
chat.nothingYet: Ask something to begin. Later questions may refer back to earlier ones.
chat.placeholder: Ask a question, then follow it up…
chat.offCorpus: This question is not about this library
chat.failed: This turn could not be answered.
chat.lostStream: The connection to this answer dropped.
chat.noCitations: Citations appear here once a turn has been answered.
chat.noPassage: The passage behind this citation is not stored.

explore.title: Explore
explore.intro: Walk a document's structure, the concepts it mentions, and the documents it shares them with. Nothing here spends money.
explore.noDocuments: No indexed documents in this library yet.
explore.noOutline: This document has no table of contents. Headings are only recognised when they are numbered, or when a learned profile supplies a pattern for ones that are not — re-import it with rule learning enabled to give it an outline.
explore.pickSection: Pick a section to read its fragments.
explore.noLocator: This fragment carries no locator, so it cannot be traced back to the original.
explore.noConcepts: No concepts were extracted for this version. Extraction is a paid stage and can be declined at the gate — this does not mean the document has none.
explore.noClaims: No claims about this concept clear the confidence floor.
explore.noRelated: No other document shares concepts with this one.
explore.proposedHelp: Extracted by a model rather than read from the document's own structure. The percentage is its confidence.

provider.title: Provider
provider.intro: Correction, embedding, concept extraction and answering all run on Vertex AI. Naming a project costs nothing; only the stages themselves are billed.
provider.projectUnset: No billing project named — paid stages will refuse to run.
provider.adcHow: Gemini Enterprise refuses API keys, so these are the only authentication that works. Run `gcloud auth application-default login` and reload.
provider.needsRestart: Saved. The running containers keep the previous project until you bring the stack down and up again.
provider.secretStored: stored — type a new one to replace it
provider.secretNeedsRestart: The worker reads this file at startup, so the services have to be recreated for the key to reach it.

secretIntro.youtube: Needed to read a channel's catalogue. Kept in the OS keychain and written into the secrets file the worker mounts read-only; it is never shown back.

libraries.label: Library
libraries.none: No libraries yet. Import a document and one is created when it registers.
libraries.failed: Could not read the list of libraries
libraries.notReady: This library has no indexed version, so any question falls off the corpus. Finish an import first.

graph.title: Graph
graph.intro: Which concepts bridge which documents. This is what a list cannot show. None of it costs money.
graph.empty: Pick a document and its neighbourhood in the graph is drawn.
graph.alt: Graph centred on {{title}}: its concepts and the documents sharing them.
graph.proposed: No line joins a concept to an outer-ring document. The API does say which concepts are shared — that is what the highlighting uses — but not through which chunk of each document, so a line per concept would be an invented relation. Select a document to see which ones it shares.
graph.noClaims: No claim about this concept clears the threshold.
graph.selectConcept: Pick a concept in the inner ring to read the claims behind it.
graph.hint: Hover or focus a node for its full name. Enter opens it.

compare.otherUnavailable: The other document's concepts could not be read.
compare.truncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}}: the list is truncated.
compare.partial: The shared list is complete. The two \u201conly in\u201d lists come from each document's top concepts, so what they show is correct but may not be all of it.

graph.libraryIntro: The whole library at once: every book, and the concepts that join one to another. Selecting a book lights its concepts; selecting a concept lights every book that mentions it.
graph.libraryAlt: Graph of the library: {{books}} books and {{concepts}} concepts
graph.libraryEmpty: Nothing in this library has been projected into the graph yet.
graph.libraryProposed: Every line here is a mention a model proposed, above the confidence threshold shown. The threshold that decides how much is drawn is the other one: a concept only one book mentions cannot join two books, so it is left off the canvas — it is still in the list beside it, and setting the filter to every book draws them all.
graph.clusterNote: Groups are cut from the graph itself — concepts that share books — and each is named after its own most widely mentioned concepts. Nobody assigned these topics, so read a name as a description of what the group holds rather than as a title.

overviewLegend.size: Size: how many books mention it

graph.degreeValueSome: at least {{n}} books · {{shown}} of {{total}} concepts drawn

backend.title: Backend
backend.intro: Two products, one app. The local backend is the stack on this machine: free, self-managed, reachable only from here. The paid service is hosted and multi-tenant. Both answer the same requests, so nothing else in the app changes.
backend.signedOut: Not signed in — the paid service refuses every request until you are.
backend.localNote: The local backend needs no sign-in: it is bound to this machine and has no accounts.
backend.signOutNote: Signing out forgets the session on this machine. It does not end it anywhere else.

secretStore.keychain: The session is kept in this computer system keychain.
secretStore.file: There is no system keychain here, so the session is kept in an owner-only file under the app data directory. It works, and it is protected by the file permissions rather than by the operating system.

activity.title: In progress
activity.spentLags: The stage that costs most records its spend when it ends, so this figure lags while it runs.
activity.cancelFailed: It could not be stopped. It is still running.

stage.awaiting_correction_review: waiting for the correction to be reviewed

audit.noTrail: This run predates the stage trail, so only its total is recorded.
audit.warning: The rules came from profile {{profile}}, learned from {{other}}.
audit.caveat: Prices are third-party multipliers over measured token counts. A stage with no figure did not spend; one marked “not priced” spent against a model whose price is unknown.
audit.logExpired: Temporal no longer holds this run's history. The stages above come from the catalog and are not affected.
audit.logTruncated: Only the first events are shown; there are more.
audit.logEmpty: The history holds no events worth showing.
audit.noRuns: No run recorded for this version.

channel.title: YouTube channel
channel.intro: Read a whole channel, work out which videos discuss a topic, and decide which are worth indexing. Every claim can then be checked at the minute of the video.
channel.syncCaveat: Free: it costs YouTube Data API quota, never money. The channel's catalogue is stored and its library is created.
channel.none: No channel synced yet. Paste a channel link in the bar above.
channel.topicCaveat: A title and a description are a hypothesis about relevance, never proof that the video discusses the topic. That is why the transcript is read afterwards.
channel.topicFromKeywords: The words ticked above fill this field; you can edit it. What is searched for in the videos is whatever is written here.
channel.deepLimitCaveat: The transcript cap is not about price: captions are free, but YouTube's caption endpoint throttles consecutive downloads, and a download that gives up is the branch that ends up paying for Amazon transcription.
channel.quoteFor: {{evaluated}} videos will be judged on their metadata and {{read}} transcripts will be read.
channel.quoteCaveat: This figure is shown before anything is spent and stored inside the run, so that afterwards somebody can check whether it under- or over-reported.
channel.invented: The model returned {{count}} verdict(s) about videos it was never sent. They were dropped.
channel.unevaluated: {{count}} video(s) came back with no usable verdict. They show as "unevaluated", not as discarded.
channel.probeCaveat: Probing is free: it resolves the video, downloads the captions, builds the transcript, previews the chunks and works out the cost. Nothing is paid for until approval.
channel.overCap: {{count}} ticked beyond the transcript cap: raise the cap or untick. The probes that fit still run.
channel.stageSemanticsCaveat: Ticked before probing, never after: each gate quotes the options its run was started with. Without concepts the video is indexed and citable but invisible on the graph.
channel.keywordsCaveat: Free: they come from the catalogue already downloaded. Pressing one narrows the table to videos whose title carries it and fills the topic with it. Words in more than half the titles are not offered: they are the channel's name, not a topic.
channel.keywordsNone: No title repeats a word worth filtering on.
channel.pickedWithoutCaptions: {{count}} of those selected have no captions: they must be transcribed, which costs on the order of twelve times more, and their transcript could not be read — so their only evidence is a title.
channel.unpriced: {{count}} selected have no price: their probe has not reached its gate yet.
channel.outsideFilter: outside the filter: it has a probe pending
channel.unverifiedTopics: {{count}} topic(s) with no quotation checkable against the transcript
channel.approveCaveat: Every video is a run with its own gate: approving the batch answers them one by one, anything unticked is rejected and costs nothing, and doing it again does not charge twice.
channel.askCaveat: Only over what is already indexed of this channel. The answer separates what the sermons say — every finding with its minute — from what the model infers, and says so when there is no material.
channel.interpretationCaveat: This is the model's inference over the findings above, not something the sermons say. Each one states what it rests on and what it does not allow you to conclude.
channel.demoted: {{count}} finding(s) were moved to limitations for having no checkable citation.

state.off_corpus: The topic does not seem to be about this channel
